appraisal_events.evidence: elle esquissa le sourire de joie et de surprise qu'elle aurait eu si on n'en avait jamais prononcé devant elle d'autre que celui-là... elle tendait la main d'un air hésitant destiné à prouver la réserve apprise... Aussi ses beaux-parents... déclaraient-ils qu'elle était un ange, d'autant plus qu'ils préféraient paraître... avoir cédé à l'attrait plutôt de ses qualités que de sa grande fortune.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator exposes the young Mme de Cambremer's practiced social performance as naive incomprehension of her new family's circle, and undercuts the in-laws' praise of her as an 'angel' by implying the marriage was really valued for her fortune; the closing remark from the general, unconsciously echoing an earlier embarrassing incident, reinforces the same ironic diminishment.

status_effects.explanation: She is locally diminished by the narrator's exposure of the gap between her rehearsed social poise and her actual ignorance of her husband's social world, plus the ironic undercutting of the 'angel' praise attributed to her by her in-laws.

ambiguities: The general's closing remark alludes to 'l'incident de la bobèche', an earlier episode not included in this passage window; its full ironic weight depends on context outside the supplied text, though the narration's framing ('faisant inconsciemment allusion') already signals irony toward Mme de Cambremer.
